cards.prose: Luke's Jerusalem *trodden down* is a judgment on the city, and Ezekiel shows how such a judgment goes. The slayers are told to *come not near any man upon whom is the mark*, the men who sigh and cry over the abominations, and to *begin at my sanctuary*. It starts at the house of Elohim (God), and the marked are spared.
cards.member_phrase: come not near any man upon whom is the mark; and begin at my sanctuary
cards.member_sentence: The slaying in Jerusalem begins at the sanctuary and passes over the men marked for sighing over the abominations.

cards.prose: Luke has the sword and the captivity into all nations, and Zechariah says what such a cutting leaves behind. Two parts are *cut off and die*, but *the third shall be left therein*. That third is brought through the fire and refined like silver, and Yahuah (the LORD) calls them his people, so this is a sifting and not an end.
cards.member_phrase: two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein
cards.member_sentence: Two parts of the land are cut off and die, and a third is left to be brought through the fire and refined.

cards.prose: Luke puts an *until* on the treading down, *until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled*. Zechariah's day closes with *Yahuah (LORD) shall be king over all the earth*, one Yahuah (the LORD) and his name one, so the city that is trampled is not left to the nations for good.
cards.member_sentence: On the day Zechariah describes, Yahuah (the LORD) is king over all the earth, one Yahuah (the LORD) with one name.

cards.prose: Luke's *edge of the sword* is the sword Ezekiel's watchman is posted to watch for. If he sees it come and *blow not the trumpet*, the one taken is taken away in his iniquity and *his blood will I require at the watchman’s hand*. Yahusha (Jesus) telling his disciples beforehand is the trumpet blown.
cards.member_phrase: if the sword come, and take any person from among them, he is taken away in his iniquity
cards.member_sentence: The watchman who sees the sword and does not blow the trumpet answers for the blood of those taken away in their iniquity.

cards.prose: Luke has the people *led away captive into all nations* and Jerusalem *trodden down*, and Ezekiel says what such a laying waste answers: *I will lay the land most desolate*, with the mountains of Yashar'el (Israel) desolate so that none pass through. The next verse gives the reason, all their abominations, so the ruin answers what was done in the land.
cards.member_phrase: I will lay the land most desolate, and the pomp of her strength shall cease
cards.member_sentence: Ezekiel says Yahuah (the LORD) lays the land most desolate because of the abominations done in it.
